title: Mistake #3: why your stain leaves light blotches next to every joint

slides.title: Light patches by every joint?
slides.sub: It's the glue you wiped off

slides.label: Mistake #3
slides.heading: Wiping wet glue with a rag
slides.body: A wet rag doesn't remove squeeze-out. It thins the glue and pushes it into the open grain around the joint. Dried glue seals the wood, so stain can't soak in there and those spots stay light.

slides.label: The fix
slides.heading: Let it skin over, then scrape
slides.body: Wait until the squeeze-out turns rubbery, usually 20 to 30 minutes. Lift it off in one strip with a putty knife or a sharp chisel.
slides.fix: Not sure? Wipe a test board with stain before the real piece.

slides.heading: 3 quick checks
items: Dry fit first so you know how much glue it needs.
Use a thin, even bead, not a thick one.
Sand the joint area before you stain.
slides.tip: Push the chisel away from your hand, never toward it.
